order.why: The 32 cm prong rises monotonically from near zero to 200000 stopping at 6001 and starts at 6003, while the rival 6013 is exactly 180 deg collinear on the muon line so it is a fit kink, not a junction.

The 53.8cm muon has a genuine monotone Bragg rising 45k to 125k over its last 15cm at 18001 and the 4.3cm proton stub rises 45k to 215k away to 18003, so both prongs stop away from this fully contained junction.
Two Bragg ends in one cluster (350000 at 15000, 150000 at 15005) and 15002 is the junction both point away from, seen as a clear V in the Z-Y projection.
Rule 1 at a deg-4 junction: seg 69032 rises monotonically to 192713 at 69039 and seg 69025 to 202125 at 69034, both away, and the 126 cm MIP track of cluster 16 ends 11 cm from it.
Rule 8 abstention: three unconnected groups (max 14.5 cm) spread over 200 cm with no Bragg, no junction evidence and no readable direction, so any click is as good as any other.

Abstain: no junction anywhere in the event survives rule 1; the sole multi-prong candidate 33026 opens at 138 degrees with its longer prong rising toward it, and all eight dQ/dx profiles are flat MIP with no Bragg at any end.

The only structure is a 348cm flat-MIP track entering the y+ wall and ending in a single dark-red Bragg blob at 21002 (last 8cm rising to 135k plus a 4cm 215k stub that the zoom shows is the same hook, not a second prong), so everything is hotter AT that point and rule 1 fails; no other candidate carries any positive vertex evidence, so I abstain rather than invent one.

Only real object is one 20.5cm segment; its p4 profile is flat ~50k MIP and the 75k at the 9000 end is a single 215k spike (hot-blob trap, not a Bragg), but a 1.1cm low-charge stub sits 2.6cm off 9000 like a Michel/delta at the far end (rule 3), and 9001 is the lower-z end.

Only genuine template-following Bragg is at 13001; the 13000 end is a 2 cm 250k prong joining the MIP track at a ~45 deg kink (plus blob 40009 3 cm away), so 13000 is the origin, not the deg-2 collinear (160 deg) junction 13002

Rule 1 on a single-prong cluster: dQ/dx climbs monotonically along the whole 64 cm from 3001 to a 265k proton Bragg at 3000 that tracks the proton template, so the cool low-z end 3001 is the start; 3002 is only a 154 deg fit kink 6 cm in.

Rule 1 plus geometry: 12002 is the most upstream point of the branched cluster (z=329.4), a genuine 3-prong fan (prong angles 104/62/60 deg, no back-to-back pair), nothing rises toward it, its 13.9cm prong runs 88k->136k away and stops at 12009, and the two other prongs are hot 4cm stubs; the rival 12029 was demoted because its two strong prongs leave at 169 deg (collinear trap).

Both free ends of this 27 cm cluster are hot (145k at 15001 over a 10 cm monotone rise, 190k in the last 1.5 cm at 15000) with a MIP-level middle, so the junction they both point away from is 15002; dropped one tier because the two prongs leave it at ~171 deg, the collinear trap.

The hot charge runs continuously across 21004 - 5 cm of 125-170k on the mu side then the whole 6.7 cm p segment at 100-250k - so that is one particle stopping, split by the fitter, and the two prongs are 154 deg apart; left with 20 scattered dots I took the only proton-grade one (155431), close to a guess.
A 90 cm chain of fragments runs along +z; 17002 is the deg-3 point where a 16 cm backward proton (monotone rise to 400000 at 17001) meets the forward chain, 2 of 3 prongs rising away and none toward.

Rule 1 is 2 of 2 rising away and both far ends show genuine template-following Bragg stops (25 cm muon-like at 11001, 4 cm proton-like at 11000), which one particle cannot do; the 176.7-degree chord pair costs one tier, and a 2.3 cm blip 7 cm from 11001 marks that end as the far one.
Rule 1 clean 2 of 2 at 19004 with a genuine stopping-muon Bragg (145k) plus a Michel-like 16 cm e at 19005 and a proton Bragg blob at 19000; 136 deg opening so not the collinear trap
The 130cm flat-MIP muon exits at the z=500 wall at 10000 and terminates in mid-volume at 10001 with no Bragg and a 4.7cm e stub, so 10001 is where it was created.

Split between this deg-2 lowest-z junction whose 14cm track rises away and 48036, the apex of the 40cm e-like tangle; 48036 is hot at its head and cools away, so it reads as a stopping end, but the tangle axis back-projects 25cm and 50 degrees off 49045.

The event holds one 68cm segment, MIP-flat then a clean monotone Bragg rise to 145k over the last 8cm at 15001, so rule 1 puts the origin at the cool end 15000; there is no junction anywhere and only two vertices on the one readable cluster, hence unclear.

Only deg-4 junction in a corner tangle, sitting in a dense 200-480k charge deposit with four prongs leaving in distinct directions; the apparent rule-1 violation is that single shared blob, the hot-blob trap, not four independent Bragg peaks.

The 190 cm wall-to-wall (y=199 to x=-201) structure is a tangle of sub-MIP and near-zero-charge fits, so I treat it as junk/cosmic; the only nu-like activity is the compact z~200-207 group and 65063 is the cool start of its 19.6 cm proton, but the second proton 71087 21 cm away does not share that origin

Rule 1 with 3 of 3 prongs rising away: seg10012 is flat 50-60k for 27cm then rises monotonically to 360k into 10004, so 10004 is a stopping point and not the vertex. Tier dropped one because the two long prongs are 178.7deg apart (trap 3), though a single 114cm particle would have to enter through the bottom face travelling upward.
Rule 1 / hot-blob trap: the 247k e/cm 2.4 cm proton stub leaves 11000 at a large angle from the flat 70-80k MIP pion, so this is a two-prong junction, not the Bragg peak of one track.

Rule 1 plus rule 3 at 14006: 108 cm muon leaving it stops at 14000 with a 10 cm Michel, an 11 cm proton stub rises to 212k, and the cluster-116/108 shower fan extrapolates back to it; the competing kink at 113166 has only two prongs.
